result.title: Neuro-Symbolic Graph Transformers for Hierarchical Intention Recognition from Multimodal Human Activity Sequences
result.summary: Proactive human-robot collaboration requires autonomous systems to infer not only immediate actions but also the underlying hierarchical intentions governing human behavior. Current deep learning approaches predominantly focus on flat action classification, failing to capture the structural dependencies connecting kinematic motion to high-level goals. A Neuro-Symbolic Graph Transformer (NSGT) is proposed within this multimodal framework, a Human Reasoning Graph (HR-G) is integrated into the self-attention mechanism via learnable topological biases. Furthermore, the architecture is augmented with a differentiable First-Order Logic (FOL) loss, acting as a structural regularizer by which ontological consistency is enforced across four levels: atomic actions, composite activities, Low-Level Intentions, and High-Level Intentions. Evaluation is performed on the synthesized NTU-Hierarchy dataset, a four-level ontological extension of NTU RGB+D 120, wherein existing sequences were mapped into 119,383 complex hierarchical episodes (85 actions, 16 activities, 8 LLIs, 4 HLIs). To prevent circular supervision, strict isolation between label generation and FOL constraints was maintained. In the base configuration, 91.65% top-1 action accuracy is achieved by the NSGT. When the FOL loss is incorporated into the baseline, logic consistency is improved by 3.26 percentage points to 96.67%. Through the HR-G biases, a tunable trade-off between accuracy and structural coherence is established. In the primary consistency-maximizing configuration ($λ$ = 0.5), a logic consistency of 94.59% is reached and ontological contradictions are reduced by 33%, while a robust 89.90% top-1 action accuracy is retained. Finally, interpretable reasoning evidence is provided by the learned HR-G weights, wherein transition edges are strongly exploited ($β$ trans $\approx$ +2.6) without explicit supervision.

AI.brief_summary: 该论文提出 Neuro-Symbolic Graph Transformer：用可学习拓扑偏置把 Human Reasoning Graph 注入自注意力，并以可微一阶逻辑损失作结构正则，从多模态人体活动序列中做四层级（原子动作、复合活动、低/高层意图）意图识别，并附带合成数据与一致性指标评估。
AI.relevance_reason: 其「可微逻辑损失作分层结构正则」与「注意力拓扑偏置」可能为 latent 推理状态的多层级监督、结构化状态表示及注意力权重作为可解释证据提供方法线索；但任务为人体活动/意图识别，与 VLM 视觉推理主线距离较远，迁移可行性可供核查。
